sources.title: PlayStation Cancels Live-Service Heist Shooter, Fairgames
sources.text: Fairgames , a live-service heist game from PlayStation's Haven Studios, has been canceled by Sony. A new report from Bloomberg reveals that Fairgames has been scrapped, three and a half years after its announcement. Developer Haven Studios will not be shut down, nor will there be any layoffs, as PlayStation has decided to turn the team into a support studio for other first-party projects. The decision to pull the plug on the game was made after a recent test did not meet internal expectations. “While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set,” said executives Sean Decker and John Doyle in a note reviewed by Bloomberg. “Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game.” The test being referenced here is likely one that made some waves earlier this fall. A mysterious game known as Project Espresso, which looked a lot like Fairgames, began advertising private playtests with a gameplay trailer back in September . Not much is known about those tests, but they didn't seem to be very fruitful for the team. Fairgames was announced in 2023 and has been the subject of scrutiny for some time. Some fans pushed back on PlayStation's live-service pivot during the early 2020s, as the company has always excelled with blockbuster single-player games. When Concord bombed , fans began to express even further revulsion toward titles like Fairgames. The project has also been soured by a number of setbacks, including departures of key developers and internal struggles . Fairgames' cancelation marks yet another major failure for PlayStation's live-service efforts. Concord flopped, The Last of Us Online was scrapped , an online God of War game was killed , and Marathon has been struggling since launch. Helldivers 2, on the other hand, has been a big win for PlayStation. There's some hope that maybe Bungie's decision to revive Destiny 2 could be productive , but Sony seems to be moving away from live-service. The only other major live-service game from PlayStation on the horizon is 4:Loop , a new game from JJ Abrams' studio, Bad Robot. We'll see if it suffers a similar fate as these other titles. Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

sources.text: Haven Games to "shift focus to collaborating with other development teams across PlayStation" PlayStation has cancelled Fairgames, the live-service shooter previously in development at its Montreal-based subsidiary Haven Studios. In a statement to Bloomberg , PlayStation said Haven Studios will "shift focus to collaborating with other development teams across PlayStation Studios, while also exploring new creative opportunities." No jobs have been cut due to the cancellation. According to an email reviewed by Bloomberg, executives Sean Decker and John Doyle informed employees that a recent Fairgames playtest did not meet expectations. "While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set," they said. "Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game." Haven Studios' debut game was announced in 2023, initially scheduled for release last year, and later delayed to Spring 2026. Jade Raymond founded Haven Studios in 2021, and PlayStation Studios acquired the studio in 2022. Following Raymond's departure in May 2025 , executive producer Marie-Eve Danis and Pierre-François Sapinski were appointed co-studio heads. PlayStation started focusing on the live-service market in 2022 by acquiring Bungie for $3.6 billion . Former Sony Interactive Entertainment head Jim Ryan said the company aimed to launch more than ten live-service games by 2026 . Sony reduced the value of its acquisition by $765 million in the 2025/26 fiscal year after Destiny 2 and Marathon underperformed. Earlier this year, Bungie laid off 292 employees and ended development on Destiny 2. Following the game's final update, Bungie announced plans to reinstate vaulted campaigns , raids, and destinations to restore player trust. One of Sony’s most publicised live-service failures was Concord in 2024 , which was withdrawn from sale two weeks after release. Sony subsequently closed its developer Firewalk Studios , along with Neon Koi. Koi. In 2025, Sony cancelled two unannounced live service titles from Bend Studio and Bluepoint Games. The following year, Sony closed Bluepoint, resulting in 70 job losses . Sony Interactive CEO Hideaki Nishino previously said he wanted to "revitalise" live-service projects through a combination of first- and third-party content following its string of failures. "We believe that live service games are content that attracts users on a global level, so we want to continue to revitalise the market through both first-party and third-party content," Nishino said. "We are not only focusing on promoting new releases, but also considering what we can do with older titles in the medium to long term." He continued: "With live service games, it's important to continuously provide something. The genre itself is relatively new, and I think many people are trying various things, so we also want to continue to take on challenges within that context."

sources.text: Fairgames was revealed in 2023, but nothing more was ever seen of it. A Bloomberg report says Fairgames, a PvP heist shooter announced by Haven Studios and Sony in 2023 , has been cancelled. In something of a surprising twist, a PlayStation rep told the site there will be no layoffs as a result of the cancellation, as Haven will "shift its focus to collaborating with other development teams across PlayStation Studios, while also exploring new creative opportunities." While it was announced three years ago, work on Fairgames appears to have started even further back, in 2021. Just a couple months after her high-profile split with Google Stadia , Assassin's Creed co-creator Jade Raymond announced the formation of Haven Studios , which was "working on an unannounced new IP for PlayStation." In 2022, right around the time former PlayStation boss Jim Ryan was talking about launching 12 live service games by 2025, Sony acquired the studio outright; a year after that, Fairplay was revealed to the world. But things have not gone smoothly since then. Helldivers 2 was a massive hit, but seven of those planned games were cancelled before release . Of the remaining games, one was Marathon , which endures but has not lived up to expectations, and another was Concord , one of the most famously disastrous game launches in years, which was taken offline less than two weeks after it launched, never to return. A live-service spinoff of the Horizon series, Hunters Gathering, was also reportedly rebooted after negative feedback from playtests . A partial accounting of canned multiplayer projects: The Concord catastrophe in particular seemed to shake Sony, which began reversing its live service strategy just a few months later. Fairgames itself looked to be in trouble in 2025 when Raymond departed Haven , reportedly after an external playtest left PlayStation leadership "concerned about how the game was received and its progress." The Bloomberg report says a more recent large-scale playtest produced similar results. "While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set,” PlayStation executives Sean Decker and John Doyle wrote in an email sent to Haven Studios employees. "Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game." The one bright spot to the cancellation is that no jobs will be cut because of it: A Sony rep told Bloomberg that Haven "will shift its focus to collaborating with other development teams across PlayStation Studios, while also exploring new creative opportunities." sources.title: PlayStation adds live-service shooter Fairgames to its constantly expanding graveyard
sources.text: Sony's trail of bodies is only getting longer Sony has dug up another plot in its expanding live-service graveyard, and is lowering the still-warm corpse of Haven Studios' Fairgames into the dirt. The shooter, which was revealed in 2023, has been canceled, though PlayStation says there will be no layoffs as a result of its decision to end the project. "The studio will shift its focus to collaborating with other development teams across PlayStation Studios, while also exploring new creative opportunities," a PlayStation representative tells Bloomberg , who first reported the news. Fairgames was revealed in a 2023 trailer which stylized the title as "Fairgame$." The trailer featured no in-game footage, but presented a stylish version of a Payday-style shooter focused on heists. But the game never materialized again. The last major news on the project came in 2025, when Haven Studios founder Jade Raymond – a veteran Ubisoft producer who'd worked on Assassins' Creed – left the company . Bloomberg reports that Fairgames was ultimately canceled after a poor showing during a recent test session with thousands of players. "While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set," according to an internal memo. PlayStation had apparently reworked the game multiple times since it was first revealed, and prior to the test had planned to showcase it again under a new title, according to the report. While PlayStation once had extensive plans for live-service games, it's canceled so many of those projects that it's now difficult to keep track of them all. The death of Concord just two weeks after launch is perhaps the highest profile example, but that's just the most memorable corpse among an extensive trail of bodies. A multiplayer God of War title from Bluepoint and a live-service game from Bend Studio were canceled in 2025 . A multitude of unannounced projects were iced amid mass layoffs at PlayStation in 2024, including a Twisted Metal game and an original project from the publisher's now-defunct London studio. Naughty Dog 's The Last of Us multiplayer game died in 2023 . Bungie has reportedly had numerous projects scrapped since it was acquired by Sony. PlayStation has even killed not just one , but two projects helmed by Call of Duty veteran Jason Blundell. Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more Sony's biggest live-service hit in recent years is certainly Helldivers 2, but it's struggled to replicate that success – heck, it's struggled to release other online games at any scale. The publisher's annual MLB The Show series remains a staple among baseball fans, Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls seems to have found a niche among fighting game aficionados, and Marathon is continuing to survive, but these aren't the Fortnite-level hits Sony is clearly gunning for. I guess we'll never know whether Fairgames could've been a hit. Ghost of Yotei developer Sucker Punch reportedly hit with layoffs, despite selling millions and "significantly" contributing to Sony's financials Dustin Bailey joined the GamesRadar team as a Staff Writer in May 2022, and is currently based in Missouri. He's been covering games (with occasional dalliances in the worlds of anime and pro wrestling) since 2015, first as a freelancer, then as a news writer at PCGamesN for nearly five years. His love for games was sparked somewhere between Metal Gear Solid 2 and Knights of the Old Republic, and these days you can usually find him splitting his entertainment time between retro gaming, the latest big action-adventure title, or a long haul in American Truck Simulator. sources.title: PlayStation's embattled shooter Fairgames has finally been cancelled, a new report says, as live service push withers away
sources.text: After years of silence, we finally know the fate of PlayStation's embattled live service game Fairgames. The Haven-developed co-op heist shooter has been cancelled, with the silver lining that the studio is not closing down or laying off staff. According to a new Bloomberg report, the decision to cancel Fairgames was made following the results of a recent playtest. Sony told staff on Tuesday of the playtest's poor reception and of its decision to end development. "While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set," executives Sean Decker and John Doyle reportedly wrote in an email to staff. "Combined with challenging market conditions in the PvP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game." A PlayStation spokesperson later confirmed that developers at Haven will now support other teams within the PlayStation Studios group, as they continue to "explore new creative opportunities". Fairgames was initially announced in 2023 as one of several in-development live service games, as part of an initiative by former PlayStation boss Jim Ryan to create more than a dozen games that generate recurring revenue . Most of those titles were cancelled before they were even revealed, and those that made it out, such as Concord, flopped severely . Even Sony darling Guerrilla Games seemingly can't make it work, with recent reports saying the studio's Horizon Hunters Gathering - initially envisioned as a live service spin on the robo dinosaur series - will now shift into a more traditional co-op structure without live service elements. That's assuming the team can show a revamped version of the game to executives by December. The news of Fairgames' cancellation isn't surprising. The game has had a tumultuous development journey ever since its reveal. Initially set for release in 2025, the game was soon pushed back to 2026 , following the departure of studio founder Jade Raymond . Though Sony later reiterated its commitment to its remaining in-development live service titles , Fairgames was never shown to the public again. That same year, game director Daniel Drapeau left Haven - another key departure suggesting the game had difficulties and might not see release. Throughout that time, Fairgames has reportedly been reworked multiple times, with a plan for it to be re-revealed under a new name. That name is believed to be Break In, linked to a trademark Sony filed in May , but with the project cancelled, we may never know if that was the case.

stories.summary: Nintendo has defended its decision to scrub the secret appearance of Mario characters from its The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake.

sources.title: Nintendo Defends Decision to Cut Mario and Yoshi Easter Eggs From The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake
sources.text: Nintendo has defended its decision to scrub the secret appearance of Mario characters from its The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake. Hidden away inside Hyrule Castle, the game's original 1998 version included a wall of portraits that featured Mario, Luigi, Peach, Bowser, and Yoshi artwork taken from Super Mario 64. Visit the same area in Nintendo's newly-launched Switch 2 version, however, and all references to the Mushroom Kingdom have been removed. On a similar note, a selection of Zelda: Twilight Princess artwork has also been cut, having been snuck in when Ocarina of Time was re-released on 3DS. Now, Nintendo has addressed its choice to remove these Easter eggs — and said that what was once a more "carefree" approach within Nintendo to referencing other games has been reconsidered. "Certainly, at the time, when we put those there, I don't think anybody thought it was too big a deal," legendary Zelda series producer Eiji Aonuma told Game Informer . "Maybe there was a more carefree or comfortable approach to that sort of thing. "But looking at it now... given the overall way that we're creating this world and giving the player that form of expression, if they look up and they think, 'Why is Yoshi there?' We don't want that moment to interrupt their experience of the world in that way. So we're feeling a little bit differently about it this time." While some fans might feel like it's a shame to see this more carefree attitude to Easter eggs is gone, it's fair to point out that Mario 64 Easter eggs (or Skyward Sword ones, for that matter) would make less sense today. Mario 64 was launched on the same platform as Ocarina of Time, of course, while Skyward Sword was released contemporaneously with the game's 3DS port. (Maybe Switch 2 just needs a new Mario game to actually arrive?) "I do remember at the time the designers on the 3DS version were really interested in placing Easter Eggs like that throughout the game," Aonuma continued, "and the timing of the release of Skyward Sword was such that it was perfect to go ahead and include that... [But] you don't want to interrupt the player's experience by seeing something that's unrelated to what they're currently doing in the game. So for that reason, we decided not to go that way." "No hard feelings there," commented Skyward Sword director Hidemaro Fujibayashi, who returned as a producer for this remake. And one Mario reference does still survive via Talon — a character who is an obvious nod to Mario with his bushy moustache, plus red and blue overalls. Check out his necklace, and you'll see his golden Bowser charm remains intact, all these years later. Nintendo legend Shigeru Miyamoto has previously discussed the idea of the company's different franchises crossing over , and said that he wasn't a fan — except when it is Pikmin , which he wants to include wherever possible. Earlier today, Nintendo revealed that Ocarina of Time had already shifted 5.2 million copies and become the Switch 2's fastest-selling game so far. Meanwhile, players have been having fun in-game by performing everything from Linkin Park to the Titanic theme on ocarina . You can read our review of the game here , or check out our look at the Biggest Changes from the original 1998 game. sources.text: Nintendo Switch 2 The Legend of Zelda The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Well, you’ve made it. You’re finally at the most infamous dungeon in all of Zelda -dom, the Water Temple of Ocarina of Time . Good news for you: In the remake, this dungeon is far, far easier than it’s ever been. A few of the edges have been sanded down, the rooms all look far more distinct and memorable so it’s less of a mental maze, and the iron boots can be equipped and de-equipped simply by pressing down on the gamepad. Compared to the original, it’s a smooth ride. But still, this is one of the most involved dungeons in the game, so buckle on that Zora Tunic and let’s get swimming. To enter the Water Temple, you need to be wearing (no, I wasn’t joking) the Zora Tunic, which you get by freeing King Zora from his ice block back in Zora Domain. To do that, you need Blue Fire in a bottle, which you obtain in the Ice Cavern as an adult. You’ll also need the Iron Boots from that same cavern. If you haven’t gotten that far yet, back yourself up and come back to this guide later. Once you’re in the temple, remove your iron boots and float to the top. Run forward, and you’ll be in a big, open room with a bunch of doors on all four sides across four different floors, and water below you. I’m going to be referring to this as the “main hall” going forward. We’re going to be here a lot. I’ll also be referring to doors by floor and cardinal direction, so if you’re ever confused about what I’m talking about, open that map. The first thing you’re going to do is slay that Blue Tektite in front of you. Sword, hookshot, whatever you like, just get it out of the way. Next, you’re going to equip those Iron Boots, descend to the first floor, and head through the east door. Once you’re inside, remove the boots to float upward for a cutscene with your fiancee, Ruto. When it’s over, grab the Dungeon Map from the chest in front of you, and then stand on the platform with the Triforce symbol and play Zelda’s Lullaby to lower the water level. Real quick tip: There are three different spots to mess with the water level in this dungeon, and each one will raise it to a different spot. This one brings it down to the first floor, and is marked by glowy blue pillars. It might be good to make a note somewhere of which color results in which water level, just in case you ever get turned around or confused and the water level is in the wrong place. Once the water has dropped, fearlessly jump down the hole, landing in the water below so it doesn’t damage you. Now, with the water taken care of, note that one of the torches in here is lit. Stand behind it with your bow equipped and aim an arrow through the fire to each of the two torches on the other end of the room to open the door in front of you, then enter. Defeat the three Spikes by blocking their attacks with your shield and swinging your sword when they’re vulnerable to obtain a Small Key. (Din’s Fire is also usable for this puzzle). Backtrack the way you came in and head out into the main hall. There are two more aptly named Spikes out here waiting for you; get rid of them. To your left (west side, 1F) is a bombable/breakable wall. Knock that out, and use your Iron Boots to sink, sink, sink. Head down the underwater corridor and take care of the Shell Blade by hitting it with your hookshot when its mouth is all the way open. At the end of the corridor, take off the boots and rise up. In here, climb the platform jutting out of the water and use the hookshot to grapple onto the pillars ahead of you. Take down the Tektites and the Like Like (Hookshot is great here), and you’ll be rewarded with the Compass. Now, all the way back to the main hall! To the west (1F) is a block you can push forward until it drops in the water. Do that, then use the boots to sink again. Look out for the Shell Blade in the way, then rise back up at the end of the hall. You’ll find yourself in a room with a whirlpool and some statues underwater, and a chest on the other side. This looks trickier than it is. Use the iron boots to drop into the whirlpool, aiming for the center platform (the serpent’s body) stretched down the middle of the pool. Stand on the platform and use your hookshot to smack the weird gem thing in the serpent’s mouth. This will unlock the underwater grate, allowing you to enter. You might need to don and doff the iron boots a few times to swim over properly, but with some careful aiming it’s very doable. There are two more Shell Blades to fight inside, after which you’re free to take off the boots, rise to the surface, and grab the small key. Back across the whirlpool, out the door, into the main hall again. There’s a locked door on the central pillar here, directly in front of you, and you now have a key. Head inside. Once inside, step forward, turn around, and look up for a grapple point. Use your hookshot to get on the platform above. Right in front of you is a spot to stand and play Zelda’s Lullaby to raise the water back up. ( Note : the columns here are green, green brings the water to 2F! Write it down if you need to!) Before you leave this inside pillar, though, jump in the water and look down: a new gap has opened up with the water level rising. Use iron boots to drop down, where three Spikes are waiting for you. Kill them with the hookshot, then use the hookshot to hit the green switch above your head, releasing a Shell Blade. Kill that too, then remove the iron boots where it was standing to rise up into the now-open area. There’s a red rupee in a chest on the way up, as well as a gold skulltula on the wall opposite. sources.title: Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake removed Mario and Skyward Sword references to not "interrupt" players
sources.text: Thankfully, Skyward Sword's director says "no hard feelings" The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is, by most standards, a pretty faithful remake to the original game, but Nintendo wasn't scared to make changes where necessary. I was a little bummed to learn the fun references to the Super Mario Bros. series had been removed, not to mention some Zelda: Skyward Sword art that was in the Ocarina of Time 3DS remake, but with how carefully Nintendo positions every game, remaster, and remake into its existing portfolio, I'm not at all surprised. In case you aren't a Zelda historian, the original game has several Mario references including character portraits and heavy design influences on characters like Talon, Malon, and Ingo, who strongly resemble Mario, Peach, and Luigi, respectively. It makes a lot of sense as Zelda: Ocarina of Time and Super Mario 64 were both being made at the same time, but 30 years later, the remake doesn't share that same connection to Mario 64. That's why the portraits have been removed from the remake, even though it's still pretty clear Talon, Malon, and Ingo have doppelgangers hanging out in the Mario universe. "Certainly, at the time, when we put those there, I don't think anybody thought it was too big a deal. Maybe there was a more carefree or comfortable approach to that sort of thing," Zelda series producer Eiji Aonuma tells Game Informer . "But looking at it now, like if a player is coming through that area, and given the overall way that we're, you know, creating this world and giving the player that form of expression, if they look up and they think, 'Why is Yoshi there?' We don't want that moment to interrupt their experience of the world in that way. So we're feeling a little bit differently about it this time." Similarly to the original Ocarina of Time and Mario 64, 3DS Ocarina of Time released around the same time as Zelda: Skyward Sword, which explains the crossover references there. And likewise, they were removed from the new Ocarina of Time remake so as not to distract from everything else going on. "I do remember at the time the designers on the 3DS version were really interested in placing Easter Eggs like that throughout the game, and the timing of the release of Skyward Sword was such that it was perfect to go ahead and include that. So I said, 'Okay, sure,'" says Aonuma, but same as before with the Mario 64 references, "you don't want to interrupt the player's experience by seeing something that's unrelated to what they're currently doing in the game. So for that reason, we decided not to go that way." Game Informer was kind enough to consider the feelings of Skyward Sword director Hidemaro Fujibayashi, who took part in the same interview, but thankfully it's all water under the bridge. "It's really as Mr. Aonuma said. There was an underlying concept in what we were going for, so no hard feelings there," he says. sources.title: How To Get The Biggoron Sword In The Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Remake
sources.text: Nintendo Switch 2 The Legend of Zelda The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time What, Master Sword not good enough for you? You need a Biggoron Sword too? Well, okay, fine. In the Ocarina of Time remake, I guess I recommend it. The Biggoron Sword is an optional weapon obtained via a lengthy sidequest. It’s the strongest sword in the game, dealing even more damage than the Master Sword, but it’s slower, and requires two hands to wield, so no shield on the side. Still, having it around can be handy, so let’s go on a little adventure to get one. First, you need to be adult Link. It’s also helpful to have obtained the Bolero of Fire for one specific part, though it’s not mandatory. You will need to have unfrozen King Zora in Zora Domain, though, so you’ll have to have at minimum done the Ice Cavern and obtained blue fire to release him from the red ice. Oh, and you’ll also want to have Epona at the ready. The entire questline takes place in the adult era, so no need to swap back and forth between child and adult Link. As adult Link, start off in Kakariko Village by speaking to the Cucco Lady, who’s to your right when you enter town from Hyrule Field, minding her Cuccos. She’ll give you a Pocket Egg. Wait one day (or play Sun’s Song twice to speed things along) and it will hatch into a Pocket Cucco. Take that to the big house near the center of Kakariko Village where Talon is sleeping, and use the Pocket Cucco next to him to wake him up. Then, go back to the Cucco Lady and she’ll trade you the Pocket Cucco for the adorable blue Cojiro. Take Cojiro out to the Lost Woods. From the entrance head left to where Skull Kid used to hang out in child era, and you’ll find a man sleeping against a tree stump. Use Cojiro next to him to wake him up, and he’ll give you an Odd Mushroom, asking you to take it to an old lady back in Kakariko…in four minutes flat. Warning: Don’t do what I did and try to do this part of the quest right between Water Temple and Shadow Temple. The cutscene for Kakariko Village triggered as I entered, and in the time it took to play out, my timer for the quest ran out and I had to go back and get another mushroom from the guy. You can call Epona from the exit of Kokiri Forest and ride her fast to Kakariko and you’ll easily make it on time. Using a warp song like the Nocturne of Shadow will spoil your time, so don’t do it, though there’s no real reason to in this situation. The old lady is easily reached by entering the potion shop, exiting through the back door, and then walking through the backyard to the house next door. Show her the Odd Mushroom, and receive the Odd Poultice in return. You now have to return to the man in the Lost Woods, but there’s no time limit this time, so feel free to mosey at a leisurely pace. However, when you return to Kokiri Forest, the man isn’t there. Instead, Fado is waiting for you. She says some ominous stuff about humans turning into Stalfos, and gives you the Poacher’s Axe, with very little direction as to who it needs to go to. Fortunately, you have this guide! Your destination is just outside Gerudo Valley. You can cross the bridge freely if you’ve already finished the Spirit Temple, or you can use Epona to leap over the gap. The Master Craftsman is there, and he’ll take the saw from you and give you a Broken Goron Sword in return. Now we’re getting somewhere, I guess. Use the Bolero of Fire if you have it to get up to Death Mountain in a jiffy (don’t forget to equip your Goron Tunic), or just walk. You’re aiming for the summit, where Biggoron is hanging out, hammering away. Give him the Broken Goron Sword to fix, but he can’t do it without eyedrops. He hands you a prescription, which you’ll need to take to King Zora back in Zora Domain. Whew. Almost done. King Zora will give you the Eyeball Frog, which needs to go back to the scientist in the hut at Lake Hylia in just two and a half minutes. If you’ve already thawed out Zora’s Domain, this is a quick trip through the underwater tunnel. Otherwise, you’d better sprint: you can’t use Serenade of Water, or the frog will spoil. The Lake Scientist can make your medicine, but it once again comes with a timer, and this one’s a doozy. You need to get all the way from Lake Hylia to the summit of Death Mountain, and you can’t warp. Using the Bolero of Fire (or any other warp) will cut the time on your medicine down to just ten seconds, and there’s no way to get from the center of Death Mountain Crater outside to Biggoron in that short a time. Head outside the scientist’s house instead, and call Epona. Ride like the wind across Hyrule Field, through Kakariko, and up Death Mountain, dodging boulders as you go. You have a little bit of wiggle room on the timer if you get hit by rocks a few times, but don’t dilly dally. Biggoron is thrilled, and gets to work on your sword. It’s going to take three days to make, so he gives you a receipt to hang onto for the pickup. You can either go do other stuff for three in-game days, or play the Sun’s Song six times to speed things along. At the end of it, show him the receipt, and the Biggoron Sword is yours at last. sources.title: Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake sets a Nintendo record for Switch 2 with 5.2 million sales in 4 days
sources.text: It's already eclipsed the lifetime sales of most Nintendo-published Switch 2 games The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is setting records for Nintendo, with the return to Link's 1998 adventure having the company's most successful Switch 2 game launch yet. Specifically, as confirmed in a press release today, the Ocarina of Time Switch 2 remake surpassed 5.2 million sales within four days of launch. That accounts for both digital and physical copies, though the exact split isn't reported – I'd be curious to know how many fans opted for the latter to secure one of those gorgeous foil covers. Of that 5.2 million, 810,000 came from Japan. In total, "this is the highest global sales for any Nintendo-published Nintendo Switch 2 game in its first four days," Nintendo says. To put it into perspective, the delightful Pokemon life sim Pokopia sold 2.2 million copies in its first four days when it launched earlier this year, which was enough to beat the lifetime sales of many spin-offs that had come before it. Even so, that's not even half of what Ocarina of Time remake has managed at launch. Meanwhile, initial Switch 2 system-seller Mario Kart World had sold 5.63 million units by the end of June 2025 , its first month of launch – while still a plentiful number, it clearly didn't reach it fast enough to beat Zelda. Ocarina of Time's sales are so huge, in fact, that it's already beaten the lifetime sales of the majority of Nintendo-published Switch 2 games. Looking at the data as of the end of September , the only one it's not surpassed is Mario Kart World, which has now reached 16.48 million sales. Donkey Kong Bananza has been left in the dust with its 5.05 million, as has Pokemon Legends: Z-A's Switch 2 version with 4.04 million sales, and Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave with its 1.34 million by the end of its first month. Pokopia shows 4.04 million total sales, but this is likely higher in reality, as the figure doesn't include data from Japan, Nintendo notes. The Zelda remake's success is hardly surprising. Beyond the fact that this is a beautiful new version of one of the most beloved and well-regarded games of all time, Nintendo had already indicated that copies were flying off the shelves when president Shuntaro Furukawa said that it was "off to a great start." One analyst also previously reported that the Ocarina of Time remake had the UK's second biggest launch for a Zelda game based on physical sales, reaching a number so large that it's the country's biggest-selling physical game of the year. It's almost like people love buying a hard copy of a game in a box they can keep forever, huh? sources.text: Death Stranding 2! Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii! Atomfall! Sony's revealed the second wave of games coming to PlayStation Plus Premium and Extra this month, and there are some genuine big-name attractions, led by Hideo Kojima 's futuristic delivery man showstopper Death Stranding 2: On the Beach . Here's the new games coming PlayStation Plus Extra and Premium in November: And here are a couple of games coming only to PlayStation Plus Premium in November: There's a lot to recommend in that list. Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii also shone brightly last year, as ridiculous as it was. "A raucous, absurd spin-off that manages to still feel like a first-rate Yakuza game despite the leftfield setting and delightfully unhinged plot," wrote Matt Elliott in Eurogamer's Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii review . "If you can get over a difficult start and fancy a lean take on the survival genre, Atomfall delivers an intriguing tale worth discovering," Tom Orry wrote in Eurogamer's Atomfall review . But its many variables can all too easily devolve into a miserable snipe-fest," Rick Lane wrote. There's plenty to be getting on with, then. "With a very small number of eligible PlayStation Plus Premium members (less than 0.4 percent) using the PlayStation Plus app on PC, making this change allows us to focus on enhancing high-quality experiences that more of our members want to use," Sony wrote. While you’d normally assume that would mean Grand Theft Auto VI would be available to stream on phones, PCs, the web, Xbox consoles, and even TVs, it appears to be restricted to just Xbox Series X / S and Xbox One consoles. sources.text: Both platforms encourage players to pre-load the game to minimise potential delays and crashes on launch day Grand Theft Auto 6 has become the most pre-ordered game on the PlayStation Store and Microsoft Store. "[We cannot] disclose the numbers, but the point that we're making is our prior expectations obviously were aligned with our guidance, and the pre-orders are far exceeding our original expectations," Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick recently told GamesIndustry.biz . GamesIndustry.biz recently consulted experts on whether GTA 6 could overwhelm internet traffic and if pre-loading will help manage download demand before next week's release. There still might be a Day 1 patch/extra download, but if so, it'll be very incremental." Para atravessar esta paisagem perigosa, você precisará construir novos tipos de infraestrutura, dominar equipamentos especializados e enfrentar (ou evitar) as criaturas sobrenaturais que vagam pelo mundo fragmentado. Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii | PS5, PS4 Uma nova lenda começa quando você assume o papel de Goro Majima, um homem que perdeu a memória e se reinventa como um pirata em alto-mar. Embarque em uma aventura pirata intensa e moderna com um ex-yakuza que virou capitão pirata e sua tripulação, enquanto eles travam combates eletrizantes em terra e no mar em busca de memórias perdidas e de um tesouro lendário. Atomfall, um jogo de ação e sobrevivência inspirado em fatos reais, se passa cinco anos após o acidente nuclear de Windscale, no norte da Inglaterra. Explore a área de quarentena fictícia, procure suprimentos, crie itens, negocie, lute e use a lábia para sobreviver em um cenário no interior da Inglaterra repleto de personagens bizarros, misticismo, seitas e agências governamentais clandestinas. Produzido por Rebellion, o estúdio por trás de Sniper Elite e Zombie Army, Atomfall desafiará você a desvendar o sombrio mistério do que realmente aconteceu. Uma releitura impressionante da aclamada obra-prima de RPG e o início narrativo da Trilogia Erdrick. Há muitos anos, o grande herói Ortega despediu-se da esposa e do filho ao partir em uma jornada para derrotar o vilão Baramos, o arquidemônio. Ortega falhou em sua missão, e Baramos ainda ameaça o mundo. Agora, ao completar 16 anos, o único filho de Ortega é convocado pelo rei de Aliahan e recebe uma missão da mais alta importância: assumir a jornada de Ortega, derrotar Baramos e salvar o mundo. Em Trepang2, você assume o papel de um soldado fugitivo que não tem lembranças de sua vida anterior, mas possui habilidades sobrenaturais. A vingança não sai da sua cabeça, e você não medirá esforços para conseguir o que quer. Desfira golpes devastadores, esconda-se nas sombras, empunhe armas explosivas e faça os vilões provarem do próprio veneno. Revide, descubra a verdade e enfrente uma ameaça ainda mais mortal do que você. Vivencie toda a intensidade do Campeonato de MotoGP de 2026 com todos os pilotos, equipes, motos e circuitos oficiais de forma mais autêntica: pela primeira vez, os resultados do mundo real atualizam dinamicamente as classificações dos pilotos, influenciando diretamente o desempenho no jogo ao longo da temporada. Destaque-se e acompanhe sua jornada com cartões colecionáveis deslumbrantes que celebram seu progresso. Junte-se à experiência em constante expansão de Hell Let Loose: um jogo de tiro em primeira pessoa hardcore ambientado na Segunda Guerra Mundial, com batalhas épicas de 100 jogadores que envolvem infantaria, tanques, artilharia, uma linha de frente em constante mudança e um metajogo original baseado em recursos, inspirado em jogos de estratégia em tempo real (RTS). Entre na batalha em partidas de vários jogadores de 50 vs. 50 em mapas enormes. Escolha uma das 14 missões na infantaria, os tipos de unidades de reconhecimento e armadura, cada uma equipada com armas, veículos e equipamentos diferentes. Jogue como oficial, batedor, artilheiro, médico, engenheiro, comandante de tanque e muito mais para vivenciar todos os aspectos dos combates da Segunda Guerra Mundial. Cricket 26 – The Official Game of the Ashes | PS5, PS4 Com a novíssima carreira de gestão, uma equipe profissional maior e melhor, o modo Ashes mais completo e um maior controle dentro e fora de campo, graças à gameplay aprimorada e às estratégias detalhadas, o Cricket 26 apresenta u confronto épico. Soul Reaver 2 | PS5, PS4 Nesta sequência do aclamado Legacy of Kain: Soul Reaver, assuma novamente o papel de Raziel e lute para voltar, atravessando as areias do tempo, às épocas decisivas e perigosas do passado de Nosgoth em sua busca implacável por Kain. Enfrente novos inimigos enquanto desvenda os mistérios das antigas civilizações de Nosgoth e revele os planos que estão por trás da corrupção dos Pilares. Em um futuro distante, onde todos os recursos da Terra se esgotaram, estar vivo já é um pecado por si só. Condenado a uma pena de prisão de um milhão de anos, você precisa sobreviver a missões letais para ter qualquer esperança de liberdade. Morra na prisão ou viva no combate. A escolha é sua. Use Thorn, sua arma mais confiável, para dominar o campo de batalha. sources.text: The much anticipated remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time launched on November 5, and one feature has fast become a big hit: the fact that you can now play any tune you like on Link’s ocarina. Now, social media has become awash with players sharing the results. People are tackling tunes from other video game series like Final Fantasy, anime such as Dragon Ball Z, and film scores including Titanic and The Lord of the Rings. Users often put a pun in the post, usually involving Link or Hyrule. Over on X, @StevenxTCG got Link to play Linkin Park’s ‘In the End’ on the ocarina. The post proved unexpectedly popular, prompting him to follow up with a guide on how to play it yourself. On a more upbeat note, another poster responded with ‘ Macarena of Time ,’ their take on the '90s dance craze. Okay, you guys wanted the notes so here they are. I also made a video so you can follow along lol L - A - A - R - UP+L - UP+L - UP+L - UP+L - R L - A - A - R - UP+L - UP+L - UP+L - UP+L - R L - A - A - R - UP+L - UP+L - UP+L - UP+L - R - L (hold) https://t.co/BIY5vhPSPx I see your Link-in Park and raise you Macarena of Time https://t.co/tOquHvAKFa Themes from other games also proved popular. @KOPPE_lunix posted their rendition of the emotional tearjerker ‘To Zanarkand’ from Final Fantasy 10 and also shared some guidance on how to play. Video game lecturer Dr. T. Wade Langer (aka ProfNoctis) posted a duet of Link and Cloud playing Final Fantasy 7’s main theme, adding that “I want music minigames in every game now.” Another popular choice was Kingdom Hearts’ Dearly Beloved . 時オカのオカリナで ♪ザナルカンドにて/ファイナルファンタジー10 https://t.co/5TEPMNHh1Q Main theme of FF7, as performed by my favorites. https://t.co/zel7RWX0cG Link plays Dearly Beloved in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time ✨ https://t.co/CYM5kyG3N0 More recent games also got some love, with players having a go at everything from Death Stranding’s BB’s theme to Kirby Air Riders’ main theme song Starlit Journey. I played BB's theme from Death Stranding on the ocarina in Ocarina of Time #OcarinaOfTime #DEATHSTRANDING https://t.co/UdVPNZThdd Other users tried their hand at movie soundtracks. The main theme from Titanic was a popular choice, as were The Lord of The Rings movies. Naturally, Howard Shore’s ‘Concerning Hobbits’ from The Fellowship of the Ring became ‘ Concerning Hylians .’ My Magnum Opus Concerning Hylians https://t.co/h8V5Kpxkhv The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Titanic https://t.co/cji4tJti8q Among Japanese players, store and supermarket jingles seem to be particularly popular, probably because their simple melodies are suited to the ocarina. One user tackled ‘ Yobikomi-kun ,’ a catchy ditty well-known to anyone who has spent time wandering supermarket aisles in Japan. Even discount store Don Quijote (where you can buy all manner of normal and bizarre things) got a rendition of its earworm jingle for the ‘ Hyrule branch .’ 呼び込みリンクくん #NintendoSwitch2 #ゼルダの伝説 #時のオカリナ https://t.co/s2zHxJphHY ドン・キホーテ ハイラル店 #NintendoSwitch2 #ゼルダの伝説 #時のオカリナ https://t.co/VAs5MvOpTN Some users also tried playing Japan’s national anthem , prompting comments and jokes about how Link must be part of the Hojo samurai clan, because their crest closely resembles the triangles of the Triforce in Zelda. 生まれがどうにも怪しい時の勇者 #時のオカリナ https://t.co/M87OjkcsXh Perhaps predicting this trend, Nintendo also released an official Playable Ocarina . This physical replica of Link’s musical instrument comes with the added bonus that it can also be used with the game. If you play a melody towards the Switch 2’s microphone, Link in the game will play along with you. Of course, playing songs on Link’s ocarina is also a game mechanic. By finding and learning songs, Link can do all manner of useful things like fast travel and solve puzzles. Check out our guide if you are struggling to find any of the 13 in-game songs. sources.text: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake has been a huge success for Nintendo, becoming the fastest-selling Switch 2 game ever, shifting more than 5.2 million copies in four days. Nintendo announced the sales result this morning in a press release, specifying that the record relates only to Nintendo-published games. But since Nintendo's games are the most popular Switch 2 games, the fastest-selling-ever title presumably holds. It's an incredible result for a game that's been received with enormous enthusiasm. Christian Donlan awarded The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time five golden stars in Eurogamer's review , saying: "Alongside great judgement and clever tweaks, this astonishing remake has a proper ace up its sleeve." We've also already seen a jump in US Switch 2 sales because of the game's release. So much for not launching in November near GTA 6 , eh? This level of success begs the question of whether Nintendo would consider remaking more beloved old Zelda games - or Nintendo games - to replicate this nostalgia-driven effect. Are there other Zelda games that have the pull of Ocarina of Time that haven't been remade or remastered already in some capacity? If you're inspired to pick the game up because of this, or already have it, know that we've got a whole proverbial library shelf of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time guides to help you through the game.

sources.text: The Super Cucco-findin' Game in the OoT Remake depends on speed and luck Super Cuccos in Zelda Ocarina of Time Remake are part of a game given to you by Talon at the Lon-Lon Ranch. Like in the original OoT, the Super Cucco-findin' Game is all about trying to pick out the three Super Cuccos from the group of chicken-like birds, going largely by luck and by efficiency. If you can find all three, Talon will reward you with some milk straight from the ranch, so I'll explain for you how to get these rewards as easily as possible. Winning the Super Cucco-findin' Game in the Zelda Ocarina of Time Remake is about observation at first, then about speed and a little luck. To win, you need to pick up all three Super Cuccos in 30 seconds, but there are no visual indicators that actually mark them out differently from the others. With that in mind, this is the best approach to win the game and find all three Super Cuccos: There is a certain amount of luck and speed involved here, and unlike the Zelda Ocarina of Time Treasure Chest Game , there's no item that will allow you to cheat the system and effectively guarantee victory. Each attempt will cost you 10 Rupees, but if you win, you'll get A Bottle of Lon-Lon Milk, a consumable that restores hearts when drunk. He'll also sell you refills from this point on for 30 Rupees each. The more important reward is actually the bottle itself. sources.text: Rockstar divulga trailer de lançamento de GTA 6! Assista novo vídeo legendado em PT-BR A Rockstar confirmou que GTA 6 terá como alvo 30 FPS no PlayStation 5 e Xbox Series X|S. Em comunicado divulgado nesta terça (10), a desenvolvedora também revelou que o ray tracing será um recurso exclusivo do PS5 Pro — que terá melhorias visuais em relação aos demais aparelhos. Segundo a empresa, o jogo foi desenvolvido para aproveitar ao máximo o hardware da atual geração, priorizando a qualidade gráfica e a densidade do mundo aberto. A confirmação reforça uma declaração feita em agosto por Rob Nelson, chefe de desenvolvimento e co-diretor da Rockstar North, que já havia mencionado os 30 quadros por segundo durante a produção . Na ocasião, o executivo explicou que a equipe ainda precisava avaliar a possibilidade de oferecer 60 FPS no lançamento ou em uma atualização futura. Agora, a Rockstar voltou a destacar que a prioridade é manter a fidelidade visual e o desempenho previsto para os consoles. Em comunicado, a Rockstar explicou que GTA 6 foi desenvolvido do zero para os consoles atuais, com meta de 30 FPS. A empresa afirma que o objetivo é manter a qualidade visual e a densidade dos ambientes e personagens de Leonida. “ Grand Theft Auto 6 foi totalmente desenvolvido do zero para proporcionar a melhor experiência possível para a geração atual de consoles, visando 30 quadros por segundo e levando ambas as plataformas ao seu limite absoluto”, declarou a desenvolvedora. O PS5 Pro terá recursos visuais adicionais, incluindo melhorias de nitidez por meio da tecnologia PSSR e sombras com ray tracing. Segundo a Rockstar, essas funcionalidades serão exclusivas do console mais potente da Sony. A empresa também voltou a afirmar que GTA 6 terá sua melhor experiência nos consoles PlayStation 5. No Xbox, o jogo poderá ser acessado pelo Xbox Cloud Gaming e utilizará as configurações gráficas da versão para Series S. O Remote Play também será compatível com os consoles das duas fabricantes. A decisão de manter GTA 6 a 30 FPS segue um padrão dos jogos recentes de mundo aberto da Rockstar. GTA 5 , por exemplo, só recebeu suporte a 60 quadros por segundo nos consoles com suas versões para PS5 e Xbox Series X|S. Já Red Dead Redemption 2 continua limitado a 30 FPS nos consoles atuais e ainda não recebeu uma versão nativa de nova geração com uma taxa de quadros maior. O primeiro Red Dead Redemption , por outro lado, recebeu versões recentes com suporte a 60 quadros por segundo. Até o momento, a Rockstar não anunciou uma versão de GTA 6 para PC. A empresa costuma lançar seus jogos inicialmente nos consoles e disponibilizar uma edição para computadores posteriormente, geralmente com opções adicionais de desempenho e configurações gráficas. Lembrando que a Rockstar também liberou o pré-carregamento de GTA 6 nesta terça-feira (10) no PS5 e no Xbox Series X|S. A função permite baixar os arquivos do jogo antecipadamente para que os jogadores possam começar a aventura assim que o título for lançado, em 19 de novembro. Quem comprou o jogo digitalmente pode configurar o console para realizar o download automático. No PS5, é necessário ativar os downloads automáticos e deixar o aparelho ligado ou em modo de repouso. No Xbox, basta habilitar as atualizações automáticas e manter o console ligado ou em suspensão. A PlayStation recomenda reservar pelo menos 212 GB de espaço livre no armazenamento do PS5 para instalar o jogo. O acesso será liberado à meia-noite de 19 de novembro, conforme o horário local de cada região.
